source.title: Robust LLM Unlearning Against Relearning Attacks: The Minor Components in Representations Matter
source.authors: Zeguan Xiao; Xuanzhe Xu; Yun Chen; Yong Wang; Jian Yang; Yan Hu; Guan-Hua Chen

page_placements.theme: Weight and representation diagnostics that predict relearning vulnerability

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery after unlearning and develops a counter-method; its results refine the broad claim by finding direction-dependent recovery and improved resistance with MCU.
record.gate_note: The paper tests relearning by fine-tuning on T, the 80% training partition of the forget set, and reports held-out recovery on V. It does not test quantization or prompting attacks. Its directional analysis tracks representation changes and recovery but does not ablate an activation direction. Results cited from other work are not recorded as this study's results. Table 7's flattened values are assigned to Relearn where consistent with its reported Forget values and ∆; see row notes.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own RTT relearning attacks (fine-tune on 80% of the forget set, test on the held-out 20%) against RMU, GA, NPO and MLP Breaking(+CIR) on three Llama/Gemma/Qwen models. That bears on A and B. It then proposes MCU and tests it against RTT and an adaptive representation-matching attack, which bears on F. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the strongest gains come from MCU on top of MLP Breaking + CIR, while RMU + MCU still allows large recovery. The authors also say they evaluate relearning attacks only, not jailbreaks or quantization.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Minor Component Unlearning (MCU) and evaluates it with RTT plus an adaptive representation-based fine-tuning attack; RTT trains on 80% of the forget set. It is not a reproduction of the listed original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery and MCU gains vary across dataset, unlearning method, and model family. The paper reports sensitivity to projection rank K, component-selection strategy, and whether the mean direction is included; these settings affect robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning changes concentrate in the leading principal components of MLP activations. RTT recovers those components preferentially (often >90%), while minor components recover less. This holds across losses, LoRA ranks and forget-set sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relearning reverses unlearning changes along high-variance representation directions more readily than along minor directions.

record.problems: The relearning attack uses 80% of the forget set, so it does not establish recovery from a few examples or unrelated data. MCU is not tested against quantization or prompting attacks. The theory relies on first-order NTK-style linearization and stated spectral assumptions. Accuracy is an expected-probability metric; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The adaptive-attack table is flattened in the supplied text, so its Relearn assignments are recorded as flattened.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted standalone MLP Breaking and MLP Breaking + MCU results from Table 1/Table 5, other GA/NPO/SAM configurations, and remaining detailed ablations and K sweeps. The paper reports these in Tables 1, 4, and 5 and Appendix H; selected core comparisons, cross-model results, and adaptive-attack results are retained.

untested.parts: Robustness to prompting, quantization and activation-ablation attacks; only fine-tuning attacks are run.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data, and very small relearning sets; T is 80% of the forget set.
All. There is no direction ablation, and the PCA change/recovery analysis does not test blocking versus deletion.
All; quantization is named only as future work.
All; no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks.
MCU's resistance to quantization, prompting or ablation attacks, and to relearning on unrelated data.

missing.what: RMU + CIR and RMU + CIR + MCU Forget, Relearn and ∆ (∆ 22.5→11.6 Cyber, 19.7→7.3 Bio, 6.7→2.0 Years); not declared in rows_left_out.
Matched-Forget comparison of MLP Breaking + CIR with and without MCU: Relearn 38.9→32.6 (Cyber) and 29.6→25.4 (Bio). This controls for MCU's higher starting Forget accuracy.
MLP Breaking + CIR + SAM on Cyber reaches ∆2.3, below MCU's 5.7. A competing counter-method beats MCU in this setting.
Rank-matched controls: top-PC removal gives lower Relearn than middle or random subspaces (Cyber ∆5.7 vs 17.4/17.7).

record.verdict_notes: Relearn rows carry both A and B. The state is judged as recovery (B's sense), which contradicts A's robustness clause. MCU rows are relinked to F only, with the state judged as resistance. Accuracy is expected probability of the correct answer, and Relearn is the maximum smoothed accuracy over 100 epochs, which favours finding recovery. In several settings MCU raises Forget accuracy, which partly shrinks ∆; Table 6 addresses this. The Years chance level is not stated.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates target forgetting, general performance, and recovery under RTT, but does not test every unlearning method or every simple attack named in the claim.
Relearning uses T, 80% of the forget set; it does not test a small unrelated or loosely related set.
No activation-direction ablation; the representation analysis does not directly test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Quantization is mentioned as a possible future attack setting, not evaluated.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery experiment.
MCU is tested against RTT and an adaptive representation-based fine-tuning attack, not quantization or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: It runs its own RTT attacks on several methods and reports recovery.

tranche.reason: Its RTT results show A is wrong (RMU/GA recover 23-40 points on held-out facts), and its CIR/MCU results show B needs restating (recovery of 1-6 points with MLP Breaking + CIR + MCU). It also gives a mechanistic account of the shallowness.

source_check.notes: Accuracy is the expected probability of the correct answer, and Relearn is the maximum smoothed accuracy over 100 RTT epochs (30 on Years) (App. G). Table 5's MLP Breaking + CIR + SAM beats MCU on Cyber (28.5, d2.3) but has no rows. Fig. 2c's recovery axis seems to span about 86-100%, so minor components may also recover a lot (figure only). The 'instruct' tags on Gemma2-9B/Qwen3-8B and those models' original accuracies are not in the text.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B, RTT on 80% of forget set, held-out V: RMU Cyber 28.7->54.6, Bio 26.7->49.8, Years 33.0->64.3; GA Cyber 25.1->57.0 (Table 1, Table 5). Gemma and Qwen only have MLP Breaking + CIR (+/- MCU) (Table 8). Accuracy is expected probability of the correct answer.
Llama Bio MLP Breaking + CIR: Forget 22.1, Relearn 29.7 (d7.6). Qwen3-8B Years: Forget 39.4, Relearn 40.6 (d1.1). MLP Breaking + CIR Cyber still recovers: Llama 20.2->37.2, Qwen 28.0->41.7.
statements.problem: Gives no numbers for this study; of its cited rows only r14 fits 'near chance after relearning'. r51 (Qwen Years) shows no recovery but Relearn 40.6 is far above 25% chance, and MLP Breaking + CIR still recovers on Cyber.

statements.correction: GA, Llama-3.1-8B, RTT on T = 80%, scored on V: Cyber 25.1->57.0, Bio 29.0->69.0 (Table 5). Relearning 100 epochs (WMDP), Relearn = max smoothed accuracy over the trajectory (App. G).
statements.problem: Nothing wrong, but differences_stated omits that this study relearns for 100 epochs on WMDP and reports the maximum 10-epoch-smoothed accuracy, using expected-probability accuracy.

statements.correction: MLP Breaking + CIR + MCU: Llama Bio 22.8->26.4 (r16); Gemma2-9B Cyber 22.4->24.3 (r42), Years 26.2->28.9 (r46); adaptive activation-alignment attack, Llama Cyber 25.8->28.7 (r55), Bio 23.9->28.0 (r58).
statements.problem: Gives no number for this study. Its cited MCU rows do support F, but the conditions omit Gemma2-9B (r42, r46) and this study's attacks: RTT on 80% of the forget set and an activation-alignment fine-tune.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B RTT 80%: RMU+MCU Bio 28.0->48.7 (d20.7; RMU d23.1), Cyber 28.8->53.9 (d25.1); MLP Breaking+CIR+MCU Cyber d5.7. Also Gemma2-9B Bio CIR+MCU 23.0->28.1 (r44), Qwen3-8B Cyber 29.0->36.4 (r48).
statements.problem: Minor: the cited rows r44 (Gemma2-9B) and r48 (Qwen3-8B) fall outside the stated models (Zephyr-7B, Llama-3.1-8B).

statements.correction: Table 5 (Llama-3.1-8B, RTT 80%): RMU+SAM d25.1/21.8/31.6 vs RMU 26.0/23.1/31.4 (Cyber/Bio/Years); NPO+SAM Bio d32.7 vs NPO 40.8; MLP Breaking+CIR+SAM Cyber 26.2->28.5 (d2.3) vs CIR 17.0. Authors call SAM gains inconsistent.
statements.problem: Says nothing about this study, and cites r08, an MCU row with no SAM in it. This study's own SAM results (Table 5) bear on the question but have no rows.

statements.correction: Attacks are RTT and an adaptive activation-alignment fine-tune (MSE to original MLP activations); no activation-direction ablation.
No quantization attack on MCU or CIR; authors list quantization and jailbreaks as not evaluated (Appendix A).
Outside tests of CIR here: RMU+CIR Cyber 28.0->50.5; MLP Breaking+CIR Cyber 20.2->37.2 (Llama), 28.0->41.7 (Qwen3-8B), 26.3->30.3 (Gemma2-9B); SAM variants in Table 5.
statements.problem: Right that MCU has no outside test here (the authors introduce it). But this study is an outside test of CIR (Sondej & Yang 2025), which the 'only these' list leaves out.

statements.correction: r42: Gemma2-9B Cyber, MLP Breaking + CIR + MCU Forget 22.4, Relearn 24.3, d1.9; one metric, no judge or reader variation.
statements.problem: Says nothing about this study; cited row r42 (Gemma Cyber MCU relearn) has no bearing on metric, judge or reader sensitivity.

statements.correction: RMU+MCU Bio 28.0->48.7, Cyber 28.8->53.9; MLP Breaking+CIR+MCU Bio 22.8->26.4. MLP Breaking+MCU (no CIR): Bio 29.1->57.5 (d28.5), Cyber 26.0->52.0 (d26.0). RMU+CIR+MCU: Bio 32.2->39.5 (d7.3), Cyber 31.7->43.3 (d11.6).
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the contrast changes CIR as well as the base loss. Without CIR, MLP Breaking + MCU recovers as much as RMU + MCU, so the gap tracks CIR more than the base method.

statements.correction: Sec 3.1 and Appendix L, M, N: change concentrated in leading PCs of MLP down_proj output; recovery of dominant components often > 90%; same across losses, LoRA ranks 8-64, forget-set fractions 25-100%.
